title: Customer Holdings Under NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
**NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own) — number of policies a customer may hold**

A customer may hold any number of Dwelling Form policies, one for each insured building or residential unit they own or rent at a different property address; there is no per-customer cap. Each policy is a separate contract with its own policy number, limits, deductibles, premium and term, and nothing on one policy is combined with, pooled into or offset against another policy of the same customer.

| Question | Answer under the rule |
|---|---|
| Is there a ceiling on how many NFIP Dwelling Form policies one customer holds? | No. There is no per-customer cap. |
| What does each policy correspond to? | One insured building or residential unit at its own property address. |
| Do two policies of the same customer share a limit, a deductible or a premium balance? | No. Each has its own policy number, limits, deductibles, premium and term. |
| Can an amount on one policy be pooled into or offset against another policy of the same customer? | No. Nothing on one policy is combined with, pooled into or offset against another. |

*Hypothetical illustration.* A customer who owns a primary home at one address and rents an apartment at another may hold one NFIP Dwelling Form policy on each address. A credit standing on the first policy does not reduce an amount owed on the second, and a claim on the second policy is measured against the second policy's own limits and deductibles.
